question.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨1,-1,2⟩+w⟨3,4,-1⟩,\,Π:r=⟨5,3,-4⟩+s⟨1,0,2⟩+t⟨0,-2,3⟩.
$$
question.worked_solution:
From the equation of a plane in the parametric form $r=p+tv+sw$, we have that its normal vector is $n=v\times w.$ In our case, the normal vectors to $Π$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =⟨1,0,2⟩\times ⟨0,-2,3⟩ \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =4i-3j-2k \\  & =⟨4,-3,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane $Π$ in dot product form is

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨4,-3,-2⟩ & =⟨5,3,-4⟩\cdot ⟨4,-3,-2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨4,-3,-2⟩ & =19.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨1,-1,2⟩+w⟨3,4,-1⟩$ into the equation of the plane in dot product form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨4,-3,-2⟩ & =19 \\ ⟨1+3w,-1+4w,2-w⟩\cdot ⟨4,-3,-2⟩ & =19 \\ 4(1+3w)-3(-1+4w)-2(2-w) & =19 \\ 4+12w+3-12w-4+2w & =19 \\ 2w & =16 \\ w & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $q$ of the intersection point $Q,$ we substitute $w=8$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}q & =⟨1+3(8),-1+4(8),2-8⟩ \\  & =⟨25,31,-6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $Q(25,31,-6).$
